results.summary: The QTCore-A1 is an 8-bit accumulator-based CPU designed conversationally with GPT-4, featuring a Von Neumann architecture with 19 registers for memory and 1 for I/O. It is controlled via an SPI interface using a scan chain for loading programs and debugging. The processor requires an external microcontroller with an SPI peripheral to load programs and provide a clock signal.

This module provides a PWM input and generator, configurable via input pins and accessible via SPI. The PWM generator's duty cycle is set by input pins, and its output is reflected on output pins. The PWM reader's output is also reflected on output pins, with a default period of 20ms. The design can be tested by looping back the generated PWM signal to the input and verifying the configuration on the output pins.

ChipTune is an 8-bit sound generator replicating vintage video game audio hardware, featuring two pulse wave generators, a triangle wave generator, and a noise generator. It receives input via a UART interface and outputs PWM audio. The project can be tested by connecting it to a computer's COM port and sending serial commands to generate various sounds.

This project implements an 8-bit signed Baugh-Wooley multiplier, adapted from a neural network project for restricted I/O. It accepts two 8-bit signed operands via input pins and outputs the 16-bit signed product across two sets of output pins. Testing involves providing the two operands and reading the resulting 16-bit product from the designated output pins.

This ASIC provides a CORDIC-locked grid-forming reference and a linear dump-load controller for micro-inverters. It generates a 60Hz sine wave, produces bi-polar PWM signals for an H-bridge, and controls a dump FET load based on DC and AC grid voltage feedback sampled by an ADC. Testing requires a simulated or real grid-tied solar system setup with associated power electronics.

Solo Squash is a single-player Pong-like game implemented on a 640x480 VGA display driver. The game features a bouncing ball within a playfield, controlled by player input for a paddle. Tones are generated for bounces, and the design can be tested by connecting the VGA outputs to a display and providing input signals.

This is a simple 4-bit current output Digital-to-Analog Converter (DAC). It accepts a 4-bit digital input on pins 0-3 to control the output current sink on analog pin 0. Testing involves applying a 4-bit digital signal to the input pins to select the desired output current.

This project implements a stepper motor controller with a Moore state machine for speed, direction, and step type control. It supports full step, half step, and double step modes, with adjustable speeds of 1s, 0.5s, 0.25s, and 0.125s. The controller can be tested by providing clock, reset, and select inputs, and observing the output signals that drive the motor coils.

This project consists of several AND gates and serves as an introduction to Tiny Tapeout, developed using Wokwi. The exact functionality is still being explored by the author. Testing involves manipulating the input dip switches and observing the output signals.

This project is a placeholder for testing the Tiny Tapeout workflow and system, created using Wokwi. Its current functionality is minimal, serving primarily as a test case. The author states that it is just a test of the method and system, with no specific external hardware currently listed.
